page: Amazon Web Services i3en.large is a storage-optimized virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. Hardware resource allocation provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core utilizing multithreading, alongside 16 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, giving an allocation of 8 GB of memory per physical core.

A key characteristic of this instance is its storage subsystem, delivering 1250 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The network tier supports a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, while graphics acceleration is absent with zero GPUs included. The CPU instruction set includes AVX and AVX-512f, with cryptographic acceleration provided via AES extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute capacity consistent with its single physical core constraint. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1100.0 and a multi-core score of 1314.0. The PassMark CPU score registered at 2095.54, while database operations achieved 690.78 points. Memory throughput reached 96.25 GB/sec for small cached reads, dropping to 13.72 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In key-value benchmarks, Redis SET operations reached 1.65 million operations per second, with static web serving measured at 1.87 GB/sec.

The primary design tradeoff centers on the high ratio of local NVMe storage relative to CPU capacity. While compute-heavy tasks face constraints from the 2-vCPU envelope, the platform provides strong resource density for disk-bound operations. Suitable workloads include distributed file systems, NoSQL database nodes, search indexes, and log aggregation pipelines requiring high localized NVMe capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.large is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. It provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 16 GB of DDR4 system memory, and a dedicated 1250 GB local NVMe SSD volume, alongside a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect its lightweight compute footprint, scoring 1100.0 on Geekbench single-core, 1314.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 2095.54 on PassMark CPU tests, with Redis handling 1.65 million SET operations per second. While compute throughput is limited by its dual-thread architecture, the instance provides high local NVMe storage density per vCPU. This profile is engineered for disk-centric architectures such as distributed datastores, NoSQL nodes, time-series logging, and local cache nodes requiring low-latency storage capacity.
